messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — we had a prod OOM on runtime pool-3 at ~21:03 UTC. Long-context convo (~120k tokens) caused KV cache to grow and eviction didn’t keep up. Kernel stayed on fast-path, but mem spiked and process died.
Priya Nair: Saw that too on dedicated-3A earlier this week. Short repro with synthetic long chat. pprof showed most allocations from kvcache::alloc_entry hotpath.
Mateo R: Uploaded flamegraph: https://internal-graphs/redwood/flame/1739004321 — KV insert churn near top.
Priya Nair: repro collection command if anyone wants to grab the profile:
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://prod-metrics/api/v1/collect" -d '{"target":"runtime-3A","duration_s":30,"pprof":true}' | jq .
```
Jin Park: Quick question — did the kernel selector switch to an alternative GEMM when sequence length passed threshold? We had a path that mirrors KV buffers when switching kernels which could double peak RSS.
Alex K: Good call. In this incident kernel stayed on int8-gemm but we saw a reuse-scoring bug. Decay multiplier on reuse-age resets on prefetch restart which makes older entries never get deprioritized -> fragmentation + low eviction pressure.
Mateo R: Proposed mitigations:
- enable compact-on-evict when fragmentation ratio > 0.65
- add decay-cap so score = max(score * decay, min_score)
- if process is in streaming mode and batch growth > threshold, soft-throttle new streams
Priya Nair: Short-term fallback we validated: proxy slow tails to cpu-serve instance. Avoids OOM but p95 latency increases (120ms -> ~600ms). Still better than crashing for SLA.
Alex K: I’ll open INC-4578 and attach the traces. Plan: patch reuse-decay + compact-on-evict, feature-flag canary (10%), monitor p99/RSS for 24h. If stable, roll to 50%.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of kvcache-reuse-fix started by @Alex K at 1739005620. Canary = 10% of pool-3.
Jin Park: Also found batching heuristic bug: streaming batch expansion ignores `max_tokens_per_batch` when requester keeps adding partial segments -> transient batch growth that forces extra KV pages to be allocated. PR #4123 fixes guard and adds unit tests.
Mateo R: I wrote a small repro that mimics the segment append pattern, pushing to 130k tokens fast. Pushed script to infra/playbooks/kv-repro.sh and added instructions.
Priya Nair: Log excerpt from the crash: 
```
[2025-04-02T21:02:59Z] runtime[pid=2341]: kvcache: allocate_entry failed: not enough memory (requested=48MB)
[2025-04-02T21:03:00Z] runtime[pid=2341]: kernel: oom-killer invoked, exiting
```
Alex K: Next steps:
- roll the reuse-decay patch under FF to 10% (in progress)
- enable compact-on-evict as emergency kill-switch for pools with frag>0.7
- backport batching guard to stable runtime 2.x (PR ready)
- monitor INC-4578 for new occurrences, and consider automated CPU-fallback at 0.95 RSS percentile.
Mateo R: I’ll wire up an alert for kvcache-frag ratio > 0.6 + rising RSS.
Jin Park: If anyone needs me I’ll triage PR #4123 and the kernel-selector checklist.
Alex K: thanks all :thumbsup: Let’s keep the thread for updates on the canary. If the canary looks good after 6 hours we expand.
